name: Harrison A. Williams
summary: Harrison Arlington "Pete" Williams Jr. (December 10, 1919 – November 17, 2001) was an American lawyer and Democratic Party politician who represented New Jersey in the United States House of Representatives (1953–1957) and the United States Senate (1959–1982). As senator, Williams was instrumenting in passing the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Act, and legislation creating the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.
